title: One Counter, Four Tablets: How to Organize a Delivery App Station
metaTitle: Multi Tablet Stand for Restaurant Delivery Stations | iBOLT
metaDescription: Learn how to organize a four-tablet delivery app station at your QSR, ghost kitchen, or pickup counter. iBOLT TabDock stands keep every screen visible,
excerpt: When DoorDash, Uber Eats, Grubhub, and your POS each live on a different corner of the counter, orders get missed and staff attention gets split. Here is how to consolidate four tablets into one organized station that every team member can read at a glance.

spec.title: One Counter, Four Tablets: How to Organize a Delivery App Station
spec.audience: quick-service restaurants, food halls, pickup counters, and ghost kitchens
spec.problem: Restaurants lose counter space and staff attention when separate tablets for delivery apps, POS, and pickup live wherever there is room.
spec.angle: Show the counter layout, cable, visibility, and role-assignment decisions that make a multi-tablet delivery station work.

sources.label: DoorDash Merchant Tablet Learning Center
sources.use: DoorDash says the merchant tablet is used for order and store management tasks in real time.

sources.label: Uber Eats Help: not accepting orders on tablet
sources.use: Uber Eats notes that its Orders app needs to stay visible in the foreground and can pause after missed orders or offline time.

sources.label: Grubhub tablet setup
sources.use: Use as a general official setup reference for third-party restaurant tablets.
